summary: Lists requirements for robust IP/UDP/RTP header compression, drawn from the ROHC charter, working group discussions and 3GPP and 3G.IP input. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3096 lists what Robust Header Compression (ROHC) should do when compressing Internet Protocol (IP), User Datagram Protocol (UDP) and Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) headers. It focuses on keeping packets efficient and correct when links lose data, delay packets or change during handover.

what is error propagation in header compression
subtitle: Requirements for compressing IP, UDP and RTP headers on lossy, high-delay links.

tldr.problem: IP, UDP and RTP headers consume capacity on links with high error rates and long round-trip times, including cellular links used for real-time services.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists requirements for a robust header-compression scheme: preserve header meaning, support IPv4 and IPv6, limit error propagation and operate efficiently despite loss, delay and packet misordering.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3096 is a requirements document, not a compression protocol. It names ROHC in RFC 3095 as an example of a protocol designed to meet the requirements.

today: RFC 3096 is an Informational requirements memo. The batch metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes it; the memo names RFC 3095 as an example protocol meeting its requirements.

sections.title: Purpose and Link Conditions
sections.content:
The ROHC working group aims to develop header compression that performs well over links with high error rates and long round-trip times. Cellular links are a main target, and the memo also says the schemes should apply to other future links with similar properties.

The requirements cover effects on Internet infrastructure, the headers and streams that must be supported, and efficiency. They are motivated by voice over IP and other real-time services carried over cellular systems.
sections.plainLanguage: The working group needed to shrink packet headers without making communication unreliable on difficult links. This memo records the requirements for that work.

sections.title: Correctness and Supported Headers
sections.content:
After compression and decompression, a header must be semantically identical to the original. If that cannot be guaranteed, the packet must be discarded. The scheme must not require changes to existing IP version 4 or version 6, UDP or RTP implementations.

The scheme must support both IP versions and arbitrary RTP streams. It should efficiently handle Mobile IP headers and should compress headers containing IPsec subheaders. The memo notes that encrypted ESP content and cryptographic data in an AH header cannot be compressed.
sections.plainLanguage: Decompression must restore the original header meaning. The scheme must work with existing IP, UDP and RTP software and support both versions of IP.

sections.title: Efficiency and Error Recovery
sections.content:
The scheme must have low relative overhead and perform better than RFC 2508 under equivalent conditions. It must keep error propagation to an absolute minimum, so loss or damage to one header does not make later headers unusable.

The memo requires efficient handling of handover loss events lasting 150 milliseconds and context recreation when a compressor or decompressor moves to another node. It should handle moderate misordering of 2-3 packets and must not noticeably add to end-to-end delay.
sections.plainLanguage: A damaged or missing compressed header should not prevent later packets from being decoded. The scheme also needs to work through handovers without adding noticeable delay.

sections.title: Link and Transmission Requirements
sections.content:
The scheme must work under expected link-delay conditions and on paths containing two or more cellular links. It must also work, possibly less efficiently, over unidirectional links or multicast links where there is no feedback channel or there are multiple receivers.

It should allow the number of frame sizes to be restricted, since some radio technologies support only a limited set efficiently. For a residual bit-error rate of at most 1e-5, the scheme must not increase the error rate.
sections.plainLanguage: Compression must work on paths with several links and on links that cannot send feedback. It must also avoid increasing errors when some bit errors remain undetected.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
A protocol developed to meet these requirements must support packets containing IPsec headers, subject to the limits on compressing encrypted or cryptographic fields. The RFC says this requirements document itself does not add security risks.

A protocol meeting the requirements may need IANA-assigned numbers. This document itself does not require IANA involvement.
sections.plainLanguage: The requirements include packets with IP security headers, though their encrypted content cannot be compressed. This memo lists requirements only; it does not define a compression protocol.
